data.gender_notes: Nereus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Nereus is the ancient Greek god of the sea, known for his shape-shifting abilities. He is the father of the Nereids, the sea nymphs. The name Nereus carries the meaning “Sea god” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nereus usually hope their child will grow to embody sea god and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nereus has its roots in Greek mythology, adding an intriguing and rich cultural background to any Christian bearer. The association with the sea evokes feelings of mystery, depth, and potential. Ancient Greeks revered Nereus as a powerful deity, invoking his name in times of sailing or navigating unfamiliar waters. Today, the name Nereus serves as a reminder of the vast and majestic ocean, the origins of human life, and the adventures that lie ahead.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Nereus holds deep symbolism for those who value the mysteries of the natural world, the deep emotions of the human heart, or the transformative powers of the divine. As the shape-shifting god of the sea, his name represents adaptability, resilience, and the ability to weather life's storms. Additionally, Nereus is the father of the Nereids, the sea nymphs, emphasizing the connection between water, life, and creativity. Thus, the name Nereus embodies change, transformation, and potential – revealing the boundless grace of the divine.
